 Northwest Notes: Kuminga, Shannon, R. Williams, Jokic
 By Luke Adams |
 at November 17, 2026 2:16 pm 
 Timberwolves forward Jonathan Kuminga exited Monday’s win over Portland in the fourth quarter after suffering a right shoulder contusion. The injury occurred as he fell to the floor after making contact with Trail Blazers guard John Tonje on a shot attempt and took a Micah Potter knee to the shoulder on his way down ( Twitter video link ).
 Kuminga has been ruled out for Tuesday’s rematch with Portland, per the team ( Twitter link ). As Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic tweets , his absence will be felt by a Timberwolves club that has been relying him on both ends of the court with star guard Anthony Edwards sidelined. In addition to taking on challenging defensive assignments, Kuminga has contributed 12.4 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 2.8 assists per game with a career-best 39.3% mark on three-pointers this fall.
 Fortunately, Krawczynski doesn’t get the sense that the injury is a significant one ( Twitter link ). While Kuminga’s shoulder is sore, Krawczynski believes the forward is considered day-to-day and shouldn’t necessarily be facing an extended absence.
 We have more from around the Northwest:
 With Edwards out and LaMelo Ball making just 2-of-13 shots on Monday, the Timberwolves showed off their depth in a 106-98 win over the Blazers, writes Jamal Collier of ESPN .  Terrence Shannon Jr. scored a career-high 34 points off the bench on just 11 field goal attempts to help lead Minnesota to victory. “It just shows how versatile our team is,” Jaden McDaniels said. “Anybody can win. TJ won the game for us today. Tomorrow might be Bones (Hyland) . Next day, me or Ayo (Dosunmu) . Whoever it is, when it’s their time, we all just want to see them succeed and just continue to instill them with confidence.” 
 As Sean Highkin of The Rose Garden Report observes, when big man Robert Williams played on Tuesday and Wednesday last week, it marked the first time he had played in both ends of a back-to-back set since his days as a Celtic. Head coach Micah Nori explained that the team was comfortable using Williams on Wednesday because he logged just 15 minutes on Tuesday and felt good after that game. It sounds like the 29-year-old’s availability for back-to-backs will be handled on a case-by-case basis going forward, Highkin adds.
 Nuggets star Nikola Jokic wasn’t happy with his team’s effort in Monday’s home loss to Phoenix, as Johnny Askounis of Eurohoops relays. During his post-game media session, Jokic said that it’s “OK to lose” if you play the right way, but he bemoaned the fact that Denver was committing sloppy turnovers and getting out-hustled on the boards on Monday. The Nuggets were out-rebounded 51-35 by a Suns team that entered the day ranked dead last in the NBA in rebounding rate (45.7%). “We need to know who we are and what can bring us to the victory, and don’t be bored or don’t be ungrateful for your role,” Jokic said. “… For me, the victory is the most important thing. So, you just need to accept and then be the best possible player in that role.”
